To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the unsaturated characteristics are of great importance for the design of cover and basal liner system for waste containment facilities and that geosynthetics should be considered in a similar manner to soils when assessing the unsaturated zone.

the unsaturated characteristics (i.e. the water retention curve) and the hydraulic conductivity function of a geosynthetic are important for assessing the behaviour of an engineered system involving geosynthetis and soils.

the unsaturated characteristics (water retention and hydraulic conductivity) of geosynthetically reinforced soils can be significantly different to those of natural materials and can influence the performance of geoenvironmental engineered systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unsaturated geotechnics of geosynthets and the interaction of geosynthtes with soils and other materials under unsaturated conditions.
the development of unsaturated geotechnical engineering principles to assess the performance of geosynthetically engineered systems under unsaturated conditions.
the unsaturated behaviour of geosynthetically reinforced systems and its influence on their overall performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
unsaturated geotechnics is important to the geoenvironmental engineer and that the unsaturated characteristics and behaviour of geosynthetcs is important to unsaturated geotechnical engineering.
the use of unsaturated geotechnics is essential for the design of geoenvironmental systems involving geosynthhetics and soils.
the unsaturated characteristics are important for many geotechnical engineering applications and geosynthetcs are no exception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of unsaturated geotechnics is essential to the design and assessment of engineered systems involving geosynthetis.
the behaviour of geosynthetically engineered systems in the unsaturated regime depends on the unsaturated characteristics and the interaction between geosynthetics, soils, and fluids.
the use of geosynthetis in unsaturated conditions is not a trivial matter and requires a thorough assessment of the unsaturated characteristics to ensure the performance of the engineered systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
unsaturated geotechnics is an essential tool to understand the behaviour of engineered geosystems where geosynthetices are involved.

the unsaturated characteristics (e.g. water retention curve and unsaturated conductivity function) of geosynthetically reinforced soils and GCLs are important in the design of geoenvironmental systems.
geosynthetics can be used in unsaturated geoenvironmental systems, but their performance must be evaluated in the context of the particular unsaturated system in which they are used.
